s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic headache disorder with postural exacerbation
salient_findings: Inferior displacement of the cerebellar tonsils on MRI
Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection on CTM
key_facts: 10-year history of headaches
Medical history significant for migraine
Headaches worsen upon standing
MRI Head showed inferior displacement of the cerebellar tonsils
CTM showed extradural contrast spread at multiple cervical and thoracic levels
Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection extending from mid cervical spine to mid thoracic level
No specific physical examination findings were reported
Patient is a 25-year-old female

shortlist.label: Chiari malformation type I
shortlist.why_kept: Inferior displacement of cerebellar tonsils on MRI

shortlist.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Headaches worsen upon standing and extradural contrast spread on CTM

shortlist.label: Syringomyelia
shortlist.why_kept: Ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection on CTM

shortlist.label: Cerebrospinal fluid leak
shortlist.why_kept: Extradural contrast spread at multiple cervical and thoracic levels on CTM

shortlist.label: Intracranial hypotension syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of worsening headaches upon standing and imaging findings

raw.rationale: The patient's worsening headaches upon standing and the imaging findings of extradural contrast spread and ventral cervicothoracic epidural CSF collection are consistent with spontaneous intracranial hypotension, which is often caused by a cerebrospinal fluid leak.

rejected.label: Chiari malformation type I
rejected.why: While the MRI shows inferior displacement of the cerebellar tonsils, which is a characteristic of Chiari malformation type I, the patient's symptoms and other imaging findings are more consistent with spontaneous intracranial hypotension.

rejected.label: Syringomyelia
rejected.why: There is no mention of a syrinx in the spinal cord, which is a characteristic finding in syringomyelia.

rejected.label: Cerebrospinal fluid leak
rejected.why: This is a possible cause of the patient's symptoms, but it is not a specific diagnosis. Spontaneous intracranial hypotension is a more specific diagnosis that encompasses the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Intracranial hypotension syndrome
rejected.why: This is another term for spontaneous intracranial hypotension, but spontaneous intracranial hypotension is a more specific and commonly used term.
